insights.title: More late-night activity
insights.whatChanged: 12 work sessions after 9 pm this period, compared with 7 in the baseline period.
insights.whyItMatters: Regular late sessions can cut into rest and personal time. They sometimes reflect time-zone overlap or deadlines that could be planned differently.
insights.suggestion: Check whether late work is expected, and whether core hours or hand-offs could be adjusted.

insights.title: Fewer recorded breaks
insights.whatChanged: Recorded breaks fell from 2.5 to 1.2 per day.
insights.whyItMatters: Regular short pauses help people sustain focus. Fewer breaks can mean meetings are back-to-back or the day is too full.
insights.suggestion: Ask whether the calendar leaves room for pauses and whether any recurring meetings could be shortened.

insights.title: Longer working days
insights.whatChanged: Aria's average weekday rose from 9 h to 10.8 h (+1.8 h a day).
insights.whyItMatters: Long days that continue for several weeks leave less time to recover. A check-in can show whether the workload, deadlines or staffing need adjusting.
insights.suggestion: Review current priorities together and agree what can be deferred or shared.

insights.title: Change in task completion
insights.whatChanged: Tasks completed per day changed by -15% (6.9 → 5.9) while hours went up.
insights.whyItMatters: Lower output alongside longer hours can mean tasks have grown in scope or the pace is hard to keep up. This is not a performance judgement.
insights.suggestion: Ask about blockers and whether task estimates or scope have changed recently.
